questionsToConsider: Is one axis, like introvert to extrovert, enough for your audience, or do they expect more than three results?
Does every question have a clear social, middle and quiet answer, so the scoring stays honest?
Where will people see this: a newsletter, a team social, or a landing page that needs a name or email?
guide.howToUseResponses: Look at how results spread across the three outcomes. If nearly everyone lands on ambivert, the middle answers are too tempting and the bands need widening. For a team activity, share the split as a conversation starter about how people like to work, never as a label that decides anything.
customizeSteps: Rewrite the scenarios for your own theme, giving the most outgoing answer two points, the middle one point and the quiet answer none.
If you add or remove questions, move the bands so each result covers about a third of the possible scores.
Share the link, then test all three results yourself before sending it out.

faqs.q: How does a personality quiz decide the result?
faqs.a: Each answer carries points toward one end of a scale. The total is compared with fixed bands, and each band shows its own result screen.

faqs.q: Is this a scientific personality test?
faqs.a: No. It is a light, informal quiz for fun or conversation, and it should not be used to make decisions about anyone.

faqs.q: How many questions does a quick personality quiz need?
faqs.a: Five to eight is enough when every question clearly separates the outcomes. More than that and people start to drop off before the result.

doc.title: Introvert or extrovert quiz
doc.description: Six everyday scenarios and three results: introvert, ambivert or extrovert.

blocks.title: Six quick scenarios, no right or wrong answers. Pick what you'd honestly do, and we'll tell you where you get your energy.
First, what should we call you?
It's Saturday night and it's pouring with rain. Your friends still want to go out. You...

options.label: Grab an umbrella. A night in would be a waste
Go, but suggest somewhere close by
Take the rain as a sign to stay in with tea and a film

blocks.title: The only free seat in the café is across from a stranger. What happens next?

options.label: You sit down and ask what they're reading
You smile, sit, and see if they start chatting
You take your coffee to go

blocks.title: It's your first week somewhere new. How do you get to know people?

options.label: Introduce myself to everyone on day one
Get to know the people I work closest with first
Let people come to me over time

blocks.title: At a party, where are you usually found?

options.label: In the middle of the loudest group
Moving between a few small conversations
In the kitchen with one good friend

blocks.title: After a long, busy week, what actually recharges you?

options.label: Seeing as many people as possible
Dinner with one or two close friends
A whole day with nobody to talk to

blocks.title: Your phone rings with a number you don't know. You...

options.label: Answer straight away. Could be interesting
Let it ring and wait for a message

endings.title: You're an introvert 📚
endings.bodyMd: You recharge on your own or with a trusted few. That usually comes with a talent for listening and for deep, one-to-one friendships.

endings.title: You're an extrovert 🎉
endings.bodyMd: You get your energy from other people. Busy rooms, new faces and last-minute plans leave you buzzing rather than drained.

endings.title: You're an ambivert ⚖️
endings.bodyMd: You sit in the middle. You enjoy company and can hold a room, but you also know when you need a quiet night to recover.
